title: LLM Energy Tests: sustained-inference energy and reliability measurements for LLMs on a CPU-only edge node
description:
Telemetry and analysis pipeline behind a longitudinal study of large language model inference on a CPU-only edge node. Four architecturally distinct models (Qwen2.5 0.5B, Phi-3 Mini, Llama 3.1 8B, DeepSeek-v2 Lite) were each held under continuous inference for 48 hours across six CPU frequency-capping scenarios, totalling 1,152 hours of load, 296,064 inference events and 4.8 million out-of-band wall-plug power samples at 1 Hz.

The archive contains the raw per-campaign streams (inference events, wall-plug power, per-core frequency), the fused per-event records, the indoor ambient record, the campaign orchestration, and the fusion and analysis code.

Read logs/MANIFEST.md before analysing the data. Thirteen campaigns were run and seven feed the reported results. Two of the excluded ones silently executed without an effective frequency cap and are superseded by verified re-executions. Analysing the wrong subset is the easiest mistake to make with this data. Two further cautions are recorded there and in logs/LICENSE: filenames encode the target rather than what actually completed, so spans must be checked before a campaign is trusted; and analysis_output/combined_dataset.csv.gz carries a moving average and drops rows with missing power samples, so it is built for figures and must not be counted from.
